EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: On the inverse XBTUSD contract, margin and PnL are in BTC while the contract is denominated in USD. The BTC loss of a leveraged long is N(1/P - 1/P0), which grows convexly as price falls, and the collateral also loses USD value. As price drops, each further tick consumes more of the BTC margin of leveraged longs, so liquidation thresholds bunch up and forced selling begets more forced selling. On the up side, the BTC loss of leveraged shorts is concave and bounded. On USDT-margined linear contracts, PnL is linear in price and collateral is stable, so this convexity is absent. Down-move cascades should therefore run longer than up-move cascades on the inverse contract, by more than they do on the linear contract. A general down-vs-up asymmetry (leverage effect, panic) and any general venue or era difference are main effects; the contract-design channel lives only in the interaction.

Eligibility is set by trailing RV_N at T. RV_N for the outcome uses only 5m bars in (T, T+N]. DVOL values must carry publication times at or before T.
EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.OBSERVABLE: TERM_SLOPE(T): ATM implied volatility at the short constant maturity minus ATM implied volatility at the longer constant maturity, interpolated from Deribit BTC option marks with snapshot times at or before T
EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.PRIMARY_TARGET: ENTRY_N(T): equal to 1 if annualized RV from 5m returns over (T, T+N] lies in the top tercile of the trailing 365-day RV_N distribution evaluated at T, among days whose trailing RV_N at T is not in the top tercile. EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.WHAT_NULL_WOULD_ELIMINATE: It would eliminate front-end term shape as carrying regime-timing information beyond the IV level and realized history, and would remove the case for buying chain-level options history for transition work.
EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.WHAT_POSITIVE_WOULD_TEACH: That dealer-absorbed short-dated demand encodes when volatility arrives, not only how much is priced, which gives an atomic timing mechanism for regime transitions.
EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.WHY_NOT_A_RESCUE: The prior IV-level observable is a control, not the claim. The new variable has a distinct dealer-inventory rationale, and its horizons and tenors are fixed in advance.

NORMALIZED_CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: The baseline is a logistic model of ENTRY_N on trailing RV_7d, RV_30d, the DVOL-minus-RV_30d gap and the year. The claim is the increment of TERM_SLOPE beyond that model. The first null permutes TERM_SLOPE in 30-day blocks relative to outcomes. The second is a HAR-RV surrogate path with an implied-volatility proxy built as a fixed smooth function of simulated past RV; it produces the term slope and the entry indicator jointly with no forward-looking information.
NORMALIZED_CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: BTC option dealers on Deribit are typically net short gamma in front-month options sold to directional and protection-seeking clients. When participants who expect a near-term volatility event (an unlock, a court ruling, a leverage build-up) demand short-dated protection, dealers must raise front-end implied volatility relative to longer tenors to ration their short-gamma capacity. An inverted front end therefore reveals concentrated, time-specific protection demand that realized history has not yet shown. If those participants are partly informed, the inversion should precede entry into a high realized-volatility regime. This holds beyond what the IV level relative to RV conveys, because the level mixes a broad risk premium with event timing, while the slope isolates timing.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Per-instrument mark implied volatility, strike, expiry and underlying index price at hourly snapshots, for interpolating 7-day, 14-day, 30-day and 60-day ATM IV
Hourly BTC DVOL index values for the baseline IV-minus-RV gap control
BTCUSDT perpetual 5m log returns for trailing RV controls and the RV_N outcome

NORMALIZED_CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate to high. It separates event-timing information in the IV term structure from the IV level already covered, and informs whether paying for options history serves regime work.
NORMALIZED_CARD.FALSIFIER: The protection-demand timing mechanism is rejected for regime entry if the TERM_SLOPE coefficient beyond the baseline model lies within the central 95 percent of the block-permutation null, or if top-minus-bottom quintile entry frequency is not positive.
NORMALIZED_CARD.FUNCTION: Unconditional regime-transition characterization: test whether the front-end ATM implied-volatility term slope at a daily decision time relates to entry into the top realized-volatility tercile over the next N days, beyond realized-history and IV-level controls.
NORMALIZED_CARD.HORIZON: N in {3, 7} days after each daily decision time T at 00:00 UTC
NORMALIZED_CARD.MAIN_CONFOUNDERS: Scheduled events that everyone sees on the calendar, such as FOMC or quarterly expiries, which mechanically invert the front end and raise RV without any informed demand. NORMALIZED_CARD.MECHANISM_DISTANCE_ARGUMENT: GV0R01-C006 used the IV level relative to trailing RV, which is included here as a baseline control. H01 and B2-01 used realized history only.

EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Within the down-shock regime, top-tercile INFLOW_Z shocks are compared with bottom-tercile shocks matched on shock-magnitude decile and year. The null permutes INFLOW_Z labels among shocks within year x shock-magnitude strata, which produces the full RECOVERY_6H contrast. A placebo uses inflow measured over the same clock window one day earlier, (T-26h, T-24h], to test whether a generally high inflow level, rather than shock-window inflow, drives the result.
EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Many participants with spare capital keep stablecoin reserves in self-custody or off-exchange wallets for counterparty-risk reasons. When a sharp liquidation-driven drop opens a discount, those who want to absorb it must first move USDT on-chain to an exchange deposit address. This takes blocks plus exchange confirmation, minutes to tens of minutes. The transfer is visible on-chain before the capital is fully deployed in the order book. A large net inflow in the shock window marks discount-absorbing capital in transit. Shocks met by such inflow should recover more over the next hours than equally sized shocks without it, because that additional resting demand arrives once the forced flow is exhausted. The constraint is the custody-to-exchange transfer latency.

EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.BASELINE_OR_NULL: The main-effect baseline regresses PERP_MOVE_SHARE_W on Relative near-touch depth of the Binance perpetual versus OKX spot, on Relative quoted spread of the Binance perpetual versus OKX spot, on the |Z_D| bucket, on hour-of-day and on the trailing 1h RV bucket. The claim is only the coefficient on the product of the two components, beyond both main effects. The null permutes LOG_SPREAD_RATIO within LOG_DEPTH_RATIO quintile x hour-of-day x month strata. This destroys the joint term while preserving both marginals and their coarse dependence, and it produces the full interaction statistic.
EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: When the Binance perpetual and OKX spot dislocate, cross-venue relative-value desks take liquidity on the venue where execution is cheaper, and makers on the other venue reprice passively toward the leader. Closure is split between the venues according to how cheaply each venue's resting liquidity is moved. Depth near the touch measures how far a given order walks the book. The quoted spread measures how stale and defensive the top of book already is. A venue that is only thin is walked but may refill fast; a venue that is only wide has defensive makers but deep resting size. A venue that is both thin and wide has makers who have already withdrawn and little size to absorb flow. Its price should carry a share of the closure larger than the separate depth and spread effects imply. This is a venue-structure claim about where adjustment happens, not about direction.
COMPONENTS: Relative near-touch depth of the Binance perpetual versus OKX spot
Relative quoted spread of the Binance perpetual versus OKX spot

EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Who acts: market makers quoting BitMEX XBTUSD, the BitMEX liquidation engine, and highly leveraged traders. Makers kept their XBTUSD inventory flat by hedging on fiat spot venues such as Bitstamp, Coinbase and Kraken, and they moved USD between those venues over bank rails. Makers who cannot rebalance collateral or hedge cheaply cut their displayed size and widen their quotes. Why the effect should exist: when the book is thin, each unit of volume moves price further (high IMPACT_PCT). A modest liquidation burst then reaches the next layer of leveraged liquidation prices, and the excursion compounds. On weekdays, rebalancing capacity refills depth quickly, so the same impact level should carry less tail consequence. The claim is limited to the weekend regime, where the capacity constraint binds by construction.

The first is Initial move sign: down versus up for a 5m return beyond SHOCK_SIGMA trailing-30d sigma, which captures the generic leverage effect present on any contract. EMITTED_PROVIDER_ITEMS.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Inverse contracts have a payoff in BTC terms that is nonlinear in USD, and margin is held in the same asset as the underlying. On a fall, leveraged holders of positive exposure lose twice: on the position, and on the USD value of their collateral. That pulls liquidation prices closer and makes forced closes self-reinforcing. Holders of negative exposure on a rise see their BTC collateral appreciate, which partly offsets the loss. Linear contracts lack this asymmetry. Era-wide differences such as market depth or participant mix should affect both signs similarly, and the main effect of design absorbs them.
COMPONENTS: Initial move sign: down versus up for a 5m return beyond SHOCK_SIGMA trailing-30d sigma
Contract margin design: BitMEX XBTUSD inverse BTC-margined versus Binance BTCUSDT linear USDT-margined

NORMALIZED_CARD.MECHANISM_DISTANCE_ARGUMENT: B2-05 infers flow absorption from klines. This card measures absorption at the price-level scale from book and trade data.
MISSING_OBSERVABLES: tick-level L2 updates
trades with aggressor side
NORMALIZED_CARD.NAME: Hidden replenishment at touched price levels and level break-through
NORMALIZED_CARD.NO_LOOKAHEAD_RULE: The refill ratio uses only data up to the episode end. The outcome window starts after the episode end.
NORMALIZED_CARD.OBSERVABLE: REFILL_RATIO = executed taker volume at the level during the touch episode divided by the maximum displayed size at that level during the episode
NORMALIZED_CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: BREACH_60 = 1 if trade price passes the level by at least BREACH_BAND_PCT within 60 minutes after the episode ends
NORMALIZED_CARD.WHAT_NULL_WOULD_ELIMINATE: It eliminates detectable hidden liquidity as a determinant of whether levels hold.
NORMALIZED_CARD.WHAT_POSITIVE_WOULD_TEACH: It would show that unseen passive supply governs whether price levels hold.
NORMALIZED_CARD.WHY_NOT_A_RESCUE: It does not reuse B2-05's kline-based fields. The observable is new.
